# Calibration (generated by `scripts/coverage_sim.py`)

400 simulated experiments per row; 40 tasks x 5 trials; task reliabilities ~ Beta(2,1); 300 bootstrap replicates; nominal level 95%. Monte-Carlo standard error is about 1 point.

| target | method | achieved coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pass^1 | two-stage, Jeffreys-smoothed (default) | 96.8% |
| pass^1 | two-stage, plug-in p-hat (rejected) | 96.0% |
| pass^1 | task-only percentile bootstrap | 93.0% |
| pass^2 | two-stage, Jeffreys-smoothed (default) | 99.5% |
| pass^2 | two-stage, plug-in p-hat (rejected) | 97.0% |
| pass^2 | task-only percentile bootstrap | 96.2% |
| pass^3 | two-stage, Jeffreys-smoothed (default) | 99.0% |
| pass^3 | two-stage, plug-in p-hat (rejected) | 90.2% |
| pass^3 | task-only percentile bootstrap | 93.8% |
| pass^5 | two-stage, Jeffreys-smoothed (default) | 99.5% |
| pass^5 | two-stage, plug-in p-hat (rejected) | 81.2% |
| pass^5 | task-only percentile bootstrap | 93.2% |

## Paired comparison (30 tasks x 6 trials per side, alpha = 0.05)

- Type-I error (identical reliabilities, non-inconclusive verdict): 0.0%
- Power (true drop of 0.25 per task, verdict `regressed`): 95.0%

Runtime 69s. The plug-in two-stage variant was the first implementation; this table is why it was replaced.
